chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to me, from al-Husayn ibn Asad al-Basri, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, who narrated on the authority of Khalaf ibn Hammad, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He passed by a group of people who were having blood-letting done for them. He told them: 'What would have been better for you if you had postponed it until Sunday evening, as that would be more effective in alleviating the ailment.'

key_terms.أَنْزَلَ لِلدَّاءِ: More effective in alleviating the ailment

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended time for blood-letting according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises delaying blood-letting (*hijamah*) until Sunday evening, reflecting the Shia tradition of aligning medical practices with specific times for optimal efficacy. This guidance underscores the integration of prophetic medicine (*al-tibb al-nabawi*) with daily rhythms, emphasizing that timing can enhance therapeutic outcomes. The recommendation highlights the practical wisdom found in Imami hadith, where physical health is managed through both natural means and spiritually significant moments.
